demand_analysis.distribution_type: lognormal-like bimodal; high-volume production days mixed with low-volume bridge days

safety_lead_time.comparison_action: increase — recommended 1.53 days vs SAP 0.0 days; update ERP master data

narrative: Demand for PL3__M207208F is highly bimodal: high-throughput production days (~44,000–52,000 units) alternate with low-volume bridge days (~200–600 units), producing an erratic regime with CV=0.59. Lead times are unstable (CV=0.80), clustering around two modes (short ~0.7 days and long ~2.7 days), likely reflecting two distinct delivery routes. The combined demand-lead-time uncertainty drives a safety stock of 52,213 units — 41% above the SAP baseline. An (r,Q) continuous review policy with EOQ-based order quantity capped at warehouse capacity achieves 95% service at dramatically lower total cost.
warnings: Storage constraint is binding: unconstrained EOQ (~1,478,456) exceeds max_storage_units; order quantity capped to 203,928 (= floor(256,141.48 - 52,213)).
SAP safety stock of 37,040 is below the statistically required 52,213; current ERP setting provides less than 95% service level coverage.
High demand CV (0.59) indicates erratic demand — bimodal demand pattern should be investigated for root cause (e.g. shift scheduling, batch processing).
Unstable lead times (CV=0.80) suggest two distinct supply modes; supplier performance review recommended.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Continuous review is appropriate for a high-volume, erratic-demand item where real-time inventory visibility is feasible. The fixed-order-quantity model leverages the EOQ economics while the reorder point absorbs combined demand and lead-time uncertainty. A periodic review model would require a larger safety stock to cover the review interval gap, worsening the already-tight storage constraint.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity cap is actively binding. The recommended policy uses exactly the full available space (52,213 SS + 203,928 OQ = 256,141 ≤ 256,141.48). Any upward revision to safety stock — e.g., if service level target is raised above 95% — must be accompanied by a proportional reduction in order quantity, increasing order frequency and ordering costs. If demand variability worsens, the current policy may no longer sustain the service level target within storage constraints.
research_insights.escalation_flag: No MOQ-capacity infeasibility: MOQ (9,260) + safety_stock (52,213) = 61,473, well within max_storage_units (256,141). No escalation required on this dimension. However, ERP master data update is required to raise safety stock from 37,040 to 52,213 and to set safety lead time from 0.0 to 1.53 days.
